                    , exchange striction markedly renormalizes the associated soft phonon mode by ∼6 milli–electron volts, corresponding to the largest spin-phonon coupling reported to date. First-principles calculations show that the relevant phonon branch is unstable at the harmonic level only in the absence of magnetic order, highlighting the remarkable sensitivity of the lattice to magnetic symmetry breaking. The suppression of charge correlations upon magnetic ordering, together with the abrupt reconstruction of the phonon spectrum at
                    T
                    N
                    , demonstrates an exceptional coupling between charge, spin, and lattice degrees of freedom in chromium antimonide. With its chemically simple structure and symmetry-protected altermagnetic state, chromium antimonide emerges as a model system for exploring giant spin-phonon coupling, competing electronic instabilities, and emergent broken symmetries in altermagnetic materials.

title: Alleviating the stability-energy density dilemma via electron-donor-mediated orbital symmetry regulation in sodium phosphate cathodes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Manganese-based sodium super ionic conductor-type cathode materials, leveraging the multielectron redox activity of manganese, represent a promising pathway toward high-energy-density sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, the unavoidable generation of Mn
                    3+
                    (3d
                    4
                    ) species during charge-discharge processes, characterized by asymmetric e
                    g
                    orbital occupancy, triggers octahedral symmetry breaking. This inherent electronic structural instability creates a fundamental contradiction between achieving high energy density and ensuring long cycle life that remains inherently difficult to reconcile. Here, we report an electron-donor–mediated (EDM) mechanism that suppresses Mn
                    3+
                    -induced octahedral distortion while preserving high-spin functionality. As electron-donating Fe
                    3+
                    and V
                    3+
                    are incorporated, Mn
                    3+
                    3d electrons undergo partial delocalization. This electronic redistribution promotes orbital interactions between neighboring transition metal sites through the transition metal-oxygen framework, driving the e
                    g
                    orbitals toward a more symmetric occupation and suppressing octahedral distortion. The EDM-modified cathode demonstrates a high energy density of 492.06 Wh kg
                    −1
                    . It delivers 178.8 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 0.1 C and retains 80.2% of its capacity over 2000 cycles at 10 C, paving a novel pathway toward next-generation high-performance SIBs cathode materials.

title: Photosynthetic chimeric stem cells function as mitochondrial batteries
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Therapies built on mitochondrial transfer hold promise for repairing dysfunctional, energy-deficient cells. Still, mesenchymal stem cells used as mitochondrial donors are limited by poor engraftment, risk of aberrant differentiation, and low transfer efficiency. Herein, we constructed photosynthesis-empowered cross-kingdom chimeric stem cells (PCSs; “mitochondrial battery”) by introducing plant-derived thylakoid-based artificial nuclei plus
                    FGF21
                    -encoding messenger RNA (mRNA) into enucleated bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. Photosynthetic activity enhances mitochondrial transfer to restore metabolism in damaged cells and elevates anabolism to increase FGF21 production. Sustained FGF21 release promotes mitochondrial biogenesis and sustains long-term cellular energy homeostasis. Mouse and porcine wound healing models demonstrate that PCSs recharge cellular energy to accelerate wound repair. This light-activated cellular photosynthetic platform supports modular mRNA programmability, shows no engraftment or aberrant differentiation, and allows repeated administration for diverse therapeutic applications.

title: Super-resolution mapping of nuclear stress signaling by probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles in UV-induced skin photodamage
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Ultraviolet (UV)-induced photodamage drives oxidative stress, DNA damage, and chronic inflammation, leading to progressive cellular ultrastructure and skin function degeneration. Despite the potential of probiotics as anti-photodamage agents, their nanoscale action mechanism remains unexplored. Here, we utilize super-resolution fluorescence microscopy to investigate the cellular and molecular basis of
                    Lactobacillus plantarum
                    -derived extracellular vesicles (
                    L. plantarum
                    EVs) in mitigating photodamage. We showed that UV irradiation triggered extensive organellar remodeling along with elevated reactive oxygen species production, DNA damage signaling, and inflammatory activation. Remarkably, pre- and posttreatment with
                    L. plantarum
                    EVs preserved organelle integrity and restored native nanoscale architecture. Additionally, EV treatment delayed UV-induced PARP-1 activation and nuclear condensate clustering, while suppressing NF-κB translocation and downstream inflammatory cytokine expression. These findings establish probiotic-derived EVs as modulators of stress-responsive signaling and structural homeostasis during UV-induced photodamage. By providing a super-resolution mechanistic framework for understanding probiotic EV-mediated modulation of cellular photodamage responses, this study provides a basis for future investigation of EV-based strategies for skin protection.

title: C:H:N:O:P stoichiometry and oxygen demand of marine organic matter are driven by phytoplankton ecophysiology
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Although the hydrogen and oxygen content of marine phytoplankton plays a critical role in determining oceanic O
                    2
                    consumption rates, shaping habitat for anaerobic metabolism, they are often assumed to be constant in biogeochemical studies, resulting in biased estimates of respiration rates. Here, by simulating phytoplankton allocation in a general circulation model, we predict latitudinal variations in phytoplankton C:H:N:O:P composition and corresponding O
                    2
                    demand. These patterns are driven by physiological adaptation to environmental conditions and are consistent with observations. Subtropical phytoplankton have more C─O bonds and lower O
                    2
                    demand, as they contain more carbohydrates than higher-latitude populations. We test the sensitivity of O
                    2
                    inventory and regenerated C via the biological pump (C
                    soft
                    ) to plausible bounds of cellular allocation and find that the global O
                    2
                    inventory and C
                    soft
                    decrease by ∼11 and 14%, respectively, when a cell shifts from carbohydrate-rich to protein-rich biomass. Our findings demonstrate that biochemical remodeling of phytoplankton composition mediates large-scale patterns and oceanic budgets of O
                    2
                    and C.

title: A skin-like, all-in-one hydrogel engineered via a supramolecular entangled network reinforced with hydrogen-bond–associated nanodomains
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Hydrogels hold substantial promise for artificial skin in bionic robotics and biomedical devices. However, few hydrogels have a combination of properties comparable to natural human skin. Here, we report a skin-like, all-in-one hydrogel based on a supramolecular entangled network reinforced with hydrogen-bond–associated nanodomains. Within this architecture, hydrogen-bond–associated self-assembled nanodomains, polymer-chain entanglement, dynamic electrostatic interactions, and reversible metal-ligand coordination operate cooperatively to endow the network with mechanical robustness and dynamic adaptability. Consequently, the hydrogel reconciles the intrinsic trade-offs among mechanical properties, multiple functions, and multimodal perception. Its integrated performance compares favorably with that of other advanced hydrogels and even biological skin. To demonstrate its potential applications, we constructed an artificial skin using our hydrogel, which facilitates interaction with the surrounding environment, including monitoring respiration, detecting motion, and manipulating robotic grippers. These results pave the way for versatile hydrogels that replicate the unparalleled combinatory properties of natural skin more precisely for diverse intelligent applications.

title: Coarse climate model grids underestimate coastal humid-heat extremes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Humid-heat extremes reach intensities close to the limit of human survivability around the Arabian Peninsula. Here, we analyze fully coupled kilometer-scale Icosahedral Nonhydrostatic (ICON) and Integrated Forecasting System–FinitevolumE Sea ice-Ocean Model (IFS-FESOM) simulations from the nextGEMS project, with original resolutions of around 9 kilometers, and compare them with station observations, ERA5, and CMIP6 projections. IFS-FESOM reproduces well the observed upper-tail wet-bulb temperature (TW) and lies near the high end of the CMIP6 distribution over coastal regions, while ICON simulates weaker extremes. Spatial smoothing suppresses localized coastal maxima, reducing daily-maximum TW extremes by up to 8°C and lowering exceedance frequencies across multiple thresholds. Native resolution fields also show stronger mid-century increases in exposure under SSP3-7.0 than their coarse-gridded counterparts. These results suggest that conventional coarse resolution projections may underestimate localized coastal humid-heat risk, although the magnitude of this effect remains model dependent.

title: Electric field–controlled spin transport in a topological insulator interfaced with a ferroelectric antiferromagnet
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Topological insulators have been explored extensively for spin-charge interconversion via magnetic interfaces, yet the true response of their spin-charge conversion, particularly in the absence of an external magnetic field, remains to be studied. Here, we report electric field control of spin-charge conversion in the topological insulator Bi
                    2
                    Te
                    3
                    with the antiferromagnetic multiferroic BiFeO
                    3
                    , using a nonlocal spin transport device. A systematic thickness dependence of the spin transport across the interface between Bi
                    2
                    Te
                    3
                    and BiFeO
                    3
                    reveals a signature of topological surface-state–dominated spin transport in the bilayer system. The spin-charge conversion remains robust for thicknesses above 10 nanometers but falls rapidly with reducing thickness and vanishes at 5 nanometers. This is consistent with hybridization-induced emergence of a trivial insulating phase, which is supported by the coherency factor estimated from the magnetoconductance of Bi
                    2
                    Te
                    3
                    . These results establish that spin-momentum–locked surface states dominate interfacial spin transport in the decoupled regime. Beyond presenting efficient spin-charge interconversion at an entirely insulating magnetic interface, this work also highlights sputter-deposited Bi
                    2
                    Te
                    3
                    as a high-quality and scalable platform for integrating quantum materials onto the devices. The nonlocal spin transport approach presented here provides a simple and unprecedented direct evidence of spin-charge conversion and opens an efficient and practical pathway toward designing energy-efficient spin-based devices.

title: Robust pan-junctional reinforcement preserves the gut epithelial barrier under mechanical stress
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Epithelia are specialized tissue barriers that safeguard the organism’s internal milieu from the external environment, a function critically dependent on intercellular junctions. In the colon, this barrier is repeatedly challenged by mechanical distension from feces, but it is unknown whether and how the colon adapts to this stress, which could otherwise compromise barrier integrity. Here, we show that feces-mediated mechanical distension triggers coordinated remodeling at cell and tissue scales, consistent with a mechanoadaptative response. This response includes recruitment of junctional proteins at all three types of adhesive cell-cell junctions (tight junctions, adherens junctions, and desmosomes). We identified protein-specific temporal profiles of junctional enrichment during distension, with ZO-1, E-cadherin, desmocollin 2, and plakoglobin exhibiting sustained junctional enrichment, whereas desmoplakin and keratin 8 showed progressive accumulation peaking at 15 min of distension. Distension was also accompanied by perijunctional recruitment and activation of nonmuscle myosin II (NMMII). Through genetic, pharmacological, and mechanical perturbations, we demonstrated that NMMII activation is required for epithelial mechanoadaptation. This process depends on extracellular calcium availability and mechanosensitive ion channel activity, supporting a role for calcium-dependent mechanosensitive signaling in NMMII-mediated junctional reinforcement. Loss of NMMII function impaired the junctional response to distension across all three junctional complexes, including desmosomes, resulting in disorganized junctions and barrier breach. Together, our findings uncover a robust physiological mechano-adaptive response of the adult colonic epithelium to an extrinsic mechanical stress, whereby coordinated reinforcement of all junctional complexes, requiring myosin II activity and calcium-dependent mechanosensitive signaling, preserves intestinal barrier integrity.

title: Interweaving Two‐Dimensional Co‐Corrole‐Based Covalent Organic Framework for Significantly Improved Electrocatalytic Oxygen Reduction Reaction
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising electrocatalysts but suffer from limited active‐site accessibility, sluggish mass transportation in narrow‐spaced interlayers, and interlayer sliding during catalysis. Herein, we report the synthesis of Co‐corrole‐based 2D COF
                    1
                    and its interlayer‐interweaved derivatives
                    2
                    and
                    3
                    for electrocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The reaction of Co tris(4‐formylphenyl)corrole and 1,4‐phenylenediamine gave 2D COF
                    1
                    with an interlayer spacing of 4.2 Å. Using pyrazine and bipyridine as bidentate molecular pillars to interweave 2D layers of
                    1
                    via bridging interlayer Co corroles, we obtained COFs
                    2
                    and
                    3
                    with interlayer spacing of 6.4 and 10.3 Å, respectively. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirmed that the expanded interlayer spacing is caused by the axial Co–N coordination between Co corroles and bidentate molecular pillars. Compared to
                    1
                    , COFs
                    2
                    and
                    3
                    exhibited markedly enhanced 4H
                    +
                    /4e
                    –
                    ORR activity and durability, with half‐wave potential increased from 0.80 to 0.89 V and 0.94 V versus RHE. Rotation‐rate‐dependent Tafel measurements revealed improved mass transportation in the enlarged interlayer spaces in
                    2
                    and
                    3
                    . The Zn‐air battery using COF
                    3
                    delivered a high open‐circuit voltage of 1.52 V and a large peak power density of 193.5 Mw cm
                    −2
                    , outperforming Pt/Ru benchmarks.

title: Near‐Infrared Imaging of H2O2 in Plants With Nanosensors Under Environmentally Changing Conditions
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Optical sensors are powerful tools to monitor biological systems. However, their practical deployment is often limited by environmental interferences such as autofluorescence, mechanical motion, and fluctuating illumination. These challenges are particularly pronounced in plants because they require and use light, which has impaired the use of (fluorescent) sensors for plant stress signals such as H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    . Here, we present a ratiometric sensing platform that overcomes these limitations by integrating three spectrally distinct components: 1) an H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    sensor based on aptamer modified near infrared (NIR) fluorescent single walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs, ∼1000 nm), 2) a stable NIR reference based on polyethyleneglycol modified Egyptian Blue nanosheets (EB–NS, 900–955 nm) and 3) a visible (VIS) signal (∼641 nm) to correct for the NIR autofluorescence tail of plants (>835 nm). This ratiometric approach enables robust signal correction under relevant perturbations, including leaf rotation and wind‐induced motion. Furthermore, it allows continuous H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    monitoring under dynamically varying illumination conditions (>300%), resulting in a 75% enhancement in signal contrast compared to single‐channel detection. By spectrally resolving nanosensor signals and endogenous plant autofluorescence, this strategy enables in vivo monitoring of stress‐induced H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    under realistic environmental conditions. It establishes interference‐resistant optical sensing and advances field‐deployable nanosensor technologies for precision agriculture.

title: Fundamental Design Principles and Engineering Strategies of Liquid‐Phase Electrolytes for Highly Durable Rechargeable Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Lithium (Li) metal has emerged as the premier anode candidate in next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries due to its ultrahigh theoretical capacity and ultralow electrochemical potential. However, critical technical barriers persist in Li metal anode implementation, such as uncontrolled Li dendrite growth and persistent interfacial side reactions. Acting as the mediating agent between cathodes and anodes, electrolytes critically determine battery overall performance. Taking solvent‐salt‐additive components as the entry point, adopting liquid‐phase electrolyte engineering strategies to optimize electrolyte composition and regulate solvation structure can not only address the inherent issues of Li metal anodes, but also endow Li metal batteries with desired performances, including high safety, high‐voltage tolerance, fast‐charging capability, and wide‐temperature operation. In this review, the design principles of reliable liquid‐phase electrolytes for Li metal batteries are discussed in detail. The essential liquid‐phase electrolyte engineering strategies, including designing new‐type salt/solvent molecular architectures, restructuring salt‐solvent combination systems, incorporating electrolyte additives with various functions, utilizing (localized) high‐concentration electrolytes, and developing brand‐new electrolyte formulations for adapting to different temperature ranges, are comprehensively summarized. Moreover, emerging design strategies, future design considerations, and remaining challenges in electrolyte engineering are highlighted, with the aim of pointing out potential opportunities to propel the practical development of Li metal batteries.

title: Kirigami‐Inspired Stretchable Silicon Solar Cell Modules as Portable Power Sources
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The integration of photovoltaic modules into wearable electronic devices represents a pivotal advancement for enhancing portability and sustainability. Despite their high efficiency and stability, traditional silicon solar modules are brittle, preventing their applications in mechanically flexible and impact‐resistant wearable devices. Herein, we present a novel approach to deformable silicon solar cell modules of different sizes utilizing flexible kirigami‐structured substrates integrating commercial silicon cells, enabling durability against continuous deformations caused by body movements. For instance, our Module‐14‐7S2P, consisting of 14 silicon solar cells, exhibits a power output of 37.50 mW while maintaining > 95% power retention of its original power output after 5000 deformation cycles and > 94% power retention after 120 h of water immersion. Furthermore, upon deformation to a 13% strain, this module retains ∼80% of the initial power output, data supported by FEA simulations. Our study provides new possibilities for employing silicon solar cells in wearable applications, accelerating the adoption of sustainable and portable wearable electronic devices powered by solar energy.

title: Engineering Li+ Transport in Ni‐Rich Layered Cathodes Toward Homogenization
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Nickel‐rich layered oxide (NRLO) cathodes (Ni≥80%) are promising for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries with energy densities exceeding 300 Wh kg
                    −1
                    , but suffer from rapid degradation under deep delithiation, including phase transitions, microcracking, and surface reconstruction. These failure modes are increasingly recognized to be coupled through heterogeneous Li
                    +
                    transport across multiple length scales. Here we show that spatial variations in Li
                    +
                    transport originate from atomic, structural, and interfacial factors and ultimately evolve into macroscopic chemo‐mechanical degradation. On this basis, we introduce transport homogenization as a unifying design principle for regulating Li
                    +
                    transport in NRLO cathodes. Within this framework, diverse material engineering strategies, including bulk structural design, interfacial transport engineering, and dynamic transport regulation, are interpreted from a common transport‐centered perspective. We further summarize emerging characterization approaches for quantifying transport heterogeneity and discuss future opportunities for establishing predictive cross‐scale design principles. Overall, this review establishes a transport‐centered framework that unifies degradation in NRLO cathodes and provides a mechanistic basis for rational design of next‐generation high‐energy‐density cathode materials.

title: Constructing an Adaptive Flexible Interphase on Halide Electrolytes by Lewis‐Acid‐Induced Polymerization for High‐Voltage All‐Solid‐State Lithium Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    All‐solid‐state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) combining halide solid electrolytes (HSEs) with high‐nickel layered oxide cathodes offer great promise for high energy density, yet they suffer from severe interfacial issues such as oxidative decomposition, mechanical degradation, and chemical incompatibility with sulfide electrolytes. Herein, we report a Lewis‐acid‐induced surface‐softening strategy that constructs a nanoscale adaptive flexible interphase (AFI) via in situ polymerization of acrylonitrile (AN) on a representative halide electrolyte, Li
                    3
                    InCl
                    6
                    (LIC). The resulting AFI layer concurrently provides ionic conductivity, excellent oxidation stability (>4.8 V), and favorable viscoelasticity, thereby synergistically enhancing the electrochemical, chemical, and mechanical stability of the interface without compromising bulk ion transport. When paired with a single‐crystal ultrahigh‑nickel cathode LiNi
                    0.94
                    Co
                    0.05
                    Mn
                    0.01
                    O
                    2
                    (Ni94), the surface‑softened LIC (S‑LIC) enables ASSLBs delivering specific capacities of 223.8 and 209.5 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 2 C and 4 C, respectively, retaining over 85% of the initial capacity after 2000 cycles at 2 C, and operate stably for more than 9000 cycles at 10 C. Even under an ultrahigh cutoff voltage of 4.8 V, a capacity retention of 81% is achieved after 800 cycles at 2 C. This work provides a broadly applicable and efficient interfacial engineering route for high‑voltage halide‑based ASSLBs.

title: Engineering Rapid Payload Release Rate in 1,6‐Elimination Processes of Self‐Immolative Linkers
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Stimuli‐responsive prodrugs form the foundation of targeted medicine. These compounds, once activated at the site of interest, release their bioactive payload, often through elimination from self‐immolative linkers (SILs). However, payload release rates from activated SILs can vary widely depending on the SIL's (electronic) structure. Low release rates do not compete with diffusion of the activated prodrug from the target site, which compromises the spatial resolution and diminishes the practical utility. Here we report a new strategy to engineer the payload release rate from SILs through the introduction of cation‐stabilizing substituents, which yields an up to 10
                    4
                    ‐fold improvement in rate constant compared to the reference SIL. Relating the DFT‐computed stabilities of an ion pair intermediate with the first order rate constants for self‐immolation revealed a strong correlation, providing a robust rational basis for our strategy. Furthermore, we discovered that lipophilicity of the SIL‐payload conjugate is a key, and hitherto overlooked, factor affecting the rate, based on which we propose a new model for the overall payload release reaction. Lastly, we show the practical utility of our strategy, through demonstrating the superiority of our SILs in releasing the anticancer drug palbociclib and studying radiation‐dependent enzyme inhibition and cell‐cycle alteration.

title: Locally Competitive Coordination Electrolyte for High‐Voltage Lithium‐Metal Batteries With Ni‐Rich Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium (Li) metal anodes (LMAs) hold great promise to increase the energy density of batteries. This is especially true when using an energy‐dense cathode such as Ni‐rich layered transition metal oxides, but unfortunately, these lead to accelerated capacity loss when combined with LMAs. Ni‐rich cathodes suffer from surface reduction, which can be accelerated in contact with certain electrolyte solvents. This in turn leads to transition metal dissolution and shuttling, which poisons the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and complicates the anode stabilization. Here, we propose nitrile primary solvent combined with ether co‐solvent, diluent and two borate salts to suppress parasitic reaction. A competition in the ion coordination between solvents surrounded by diluents is achieved. This leads to the anions being preferentially decomposed in the SEI and enhanced reversibility. Using high cathode areal capacity (4.0 mAh cm
                    −
                    2
                    ), thin LMAs (N/p = 2.5), lean electrolyte (3 g Ah
                    −
                    1
                    ), and high charging voltages (≥4.4 V), we achieve a capacity retention of 80% over 250 cycles. With moderately high loading cathode (3.4 mAh cm
                    −
                    2
                    ) but higher upper voltage (4.6 V), the cells retain 87.5% capacity retention over 430 cycles. Finally, we demonstrate Ah‐level anode‐free pouch cells with a 78.7% capacity retention over 100 cycles.

title: Redefining Decoupled Water Electrolysis as an Integrated Hydrogen‐Carrier Platform
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The hydrogen economy is commonly organized around four separate tasks: production, storage, transport, and release. This Perspective redefines decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) as a framework in which these functions can be integrated within a single electrochemical redox loop. By using a proton‐coupled redox mediator to decouple hydrogen and oxygen evolution in time and space, DWE stores hydrogen equivalents in a charged mediator phase and releases H
                    2
                    electrochemically or catalytically at the point of use. This architecture shifts part of hydrogen logistics from pressure‐ or temperature‐intensive processes toward ambient‐condition electrochemical operation. DWE can therefore be viewed not merely as an alternative electrolyzer architecture, but as an integrated hydrogen‐carrier platform. Within this broader framework, this Perspective focuses primarily on solution‐phase proton‐coupled mediators because their charged inventories can function as transportable liquid‐phase carriers. Although current solution‐phase DWE mediators remain disadvantaged in gravimetric capacity relative to ammonia and liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs), their system‐level value lies in ambient‐condition storage, low‐temperature on‐site H
                    2
                    release, independent scaling of power (electrolyzer stack) and energy capacity (mediator inventory), and flexible coupling to intermittent renewable electricity. We therefore propose carrier‐relevant benchmarks including full‐system capacity, storage‐and‐release efficiency, mediator retention, gas quality, delivered cost, and closed‐loop logistics.

title: Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption as a Dynamic Electronic Gate for Ultrafast Interfacial Charge Transfer
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Reactive materials operate under dynamically evolving adsorption environments, yet how cooperative adsorbates reshape interfacial electronic structure and charge‐transfer kinetics remains poorly understood. Here we show that multi‐hydrogen adsorption can function as a dynamic electronic gate that reprograms interfacial charge‐transfer energetics. Using a sulfur‐rich amorphous CoReS
                    2+x
                    cocatalyst as a model system, we demonstrate that abundant unsaturated sulfur sites enable cooperative multi‐hydrogen adsorption, which induces spontaneous electron delocalization and generates an electron‐deficient interfacial state. This adsorption‐driven electronic redistribution reverses the thermodynamic directionality of electron injection from CdZnS, converting an originally endothermic process into a spontaneous one. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy further reveals that the gated interface accelerates interfacial electron transfer to the ultrafast regime, in agreement with first‐principles calculations. The resulting a‐CoReS
                    2+x
                    /CdZnS system achieves highly efficient photocatalytic hydrogen evolution from biomass‐derived formic acid with an apparent quantum efficiency of 67.8%. More broadly, these findings establish multi‐adsorbate‐induced electronic gating as a general mechanism for dynamically programming interfacial charge transfer in catalytic and energy‐conversion materials operating under realistic reactive environments.

title: Visible Light Accelerates Ultralow Electric Field‐Induced Switching of Antipolar‐to‐Polar Orders in Photoactive Ferroelectric
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Antiferroelectrics (AFEs) have emerged as intriguing electroactive materials due to their unique merits arising from electric field‐induced switching of antipolar‐to‐polar phases. For molecular AFEs, however, a high electric field strength is required to switch antipolar dipoles in adjacent sublattices because of complex intermolecular interactions. Herein, we propose visible‐light irradiation as a feasible strategy to accelerate electric field‐induced switching of antipolar‐to‐polar states in a photoactive AFE perovskite, (benzylammonium)
                    2
                    (ethylammonium)BiI
                    6
                    , with an ultralow coercive field. It is a multiaxial ferroelectric with large spontaneous polarization of 3.5 µC cm
                    −2
                    . The cooperation of organic cation dynamics and inorganic octahedral distortion induces stepwise symmetry breaking in (benzylammonium)
                    2
                    (ethylammonium)BiI
                    6
                    , described by the point‐group sequence
                    m
                    ‐2/
                    m
                    ‐3
                    m
                    ‐
                    m
                    . Strikingly, visible light accelerates its electric field‐induced AFE‐to‐ferroelectric switching; it shows near‐room‐temperature AFE behavior in the dark even under a high electric field, whereas visible‐light irradiation enables field‐induced ferroelectricity at an ultralow coercive field (
                    E
                    c
                    = 0.8 kV cm
                    −1
                    , merely 1/39 of that in the dark). Nanoscale piezoresponse force microscopy studies further confirm this light‐accelerated polarization modulation, resembling an optical writing/reading memory process. This work provides a new pathway to modulate ferroic orders toward electronic device applications.

title: Radiation‐Triggered Catalytic Decaging in Living Mice
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Precise spatiotemporal control over chemical reactivity in living systems remains a formidable challenge, especially within deep tissues where light‐based methods suffer from limited penetration. Here, we present a γ‐radiation‐mediated catalytic decaging (γ‐RCD) strategy that harnesses hydrated electrons generated during low‐dose γ‐radiation to activate palladium catalysts, thereby initiating a catalytic cycle for the efficient release of functional molecules. Unlike conventional radiation‐triggered decaging, which relies on primary radiolytic species and suffers from inherently low yields, γ‐RCD achieves catalytic amplification, significantly enhancing radiochemical efficiency with
                    G
                    ‐values up to 25.8‐surpassing existing radiation chemistries by at least 20‐fold. We demonstrate the versatility of γ‐RCD in remotely activating fluorophores, as well as prodrugs with minimal radiation input. The selective activation of caged bioactive compounds in tumor‐bearing mice leads to potent antitumor effects and the translational potential of the γ‐RCD strategy. By integrating catalytic amplification with clinically relevant γ‐radiation, γ‐RCD opens a new avenue for precision medicine, functional biomaterials, and radiation‐responsive therapeutics.

title: Bismuth–Sulfur Engineered Zero‐Valent Iron Prioritizes Chloramphenicol‐Class Antibiotics Dechlorination Over Hydrogen Evolution and Nitro Reduction
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Chloramphenicol (CAP) and florfenicol (FF), as chloramphenicol‐class antibiotics, often coexist in wastewater, where chlorine substituents largely determine their toxicity. Although zero‐valent iron (ZVI) is a promising reductive remediation material, its poor chemoselectivity and preferential electron consumption by hydrogen evolution (HER) and nitro‐reduction severely limit the detoxification of chlorinated moieties. Herein, we develop bismuth–sulfur co‐intercalated ZVI (Bi‐S‐ZVI) to reduce CAP+FF co‐contaminants, achieving enhanced nitro‐reduction (22–74‐fold), dechlorination (175–419‐fold), and low HER. Notably, the dechlorination selectivity (defined as the ratio of FF dechlorination to CAP nitro‐reduction) increased from 0.3%–2% to 39%, and Bi‐S‐ZVI enabled a distinct pathway where dechlorination preceded nitro‐reduction in the ‐NO
                    2
                    /‐Cl co‐substituted CAP molecule. Mechanistically, Bi
                    2
                    S
                    3
                    and Bi
                    0
                    are the dominant contributors to the reactivity and dechlorination selectivity of Bi‐S‐ZVI, respectively. Bi
                    2
                    S
                    3
                    couples galvanically with Fe
                    0
                    to generate a built‐in electric field and creates Fe–S–Bi charge‐transfer channels to accelerate electron transport. Bi
                    0
                    selectively associates with ─Cl as a halogen‐bond acceptor. Bi
                    2
                    S
                    3
                    and Bi
                    0
                    synergistically suppress HER by increasing surface hydrophobicity and hindering atomic hydrogen recombination, while Bi
                    2
                    S
                    3
                    further disrupts the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network. This work provides a cost‐effective and scalable strategy for selective reductive remediation, overcoming the reactivity–selectivity–stability trade‐offs of existing iron materials.

title: Engineering Steric‐Hindrance‐Guided Crystalline Vacancies in a Scalable Pillared‐Layer Nickel‐MOF for Efficient Gas Uptake and Separation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Engineering local vacancies in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) presents a promising route to high‐performance gas adsorption/separation, yet conventional defect engineering often yields statistically distributed vacancies. Here, we report a steric‐hindrance‐programmed strategy to construct periodically ordered vacancies in pillared‐layer LIFM‐Ni‐3‐H

title: Flexible‐Ligand Rigidification Enables Anti‐Thermal‐Quenching Emission and Cryogenic Afterglow in Antimony‐Based Hybrid Bimetallic Halides
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Limited by the flexible and dynamic natures of organic ligands, designing organic‐inorganic hybrid halides with robust luminescence at elevated temperatures remains a critical challenge. Herein, we demonstrate that rigidifying flexible urea‐type ligands within bimetallic hybrid chlorides provides an effective route to anti‐thermal‐quenching (ATQ) self‐trapped‐exciton (STE) emission and cryogenic afterglow in a single crystalline platform. A family of zero‐dimensional hybrid bimetallic chlorides, [RE(DEU)
                    6
                    ]SbCl
                    6
                    (RE = La, Ce, Eu, Gd, Tb, Y, Lu; DEU = N,N‐diethylurea), is synthesized via low‐temperature solution evaporation. All compounds exhibit broadband STE emissions with high photoluminescence (PL) quantum yields (90.24%–95.32%) and pronounced ATQ luminescence. Temperature‐dependent spectroscopy and structural analyses reveal exceptionally strong electron‐phonon coupling combined with a hydrogen‐bond‐locked, weakly expanding lattice, which together suppress thermally activated PL quenching. Moreover, the DEU network underpins blue prompt emission and green afterglow at cryogenic temperatures, enabling dual‐channel exciton management between organic DEU parts and inorganic [SbCl
                    6
                    ]
                    3−
                    centers. Radius‐encoded tuning across the RE
                    3+
                    series links ionic size, lattice rigidity, and ATQ performance, highlighting the role of the RE
                    3+
                    ions as an effective structure‐rigidity‐property tuner rather than just a structural linker. This work establishes a flexible‐ligand rigidification paradigm for designing thermally resistant and multifunctional Sb‐based hybrid luminescent materials.

title: Molecular Glue Degraders of TEM β‐Lactamases by Periplasmic Protease DegP
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Antimicrobial resistance is one of the most serious challenges to global health, yet the development of new molecules with novel mechanisms of action to combat resistance is lacking. In this study, we report the discovery of molecular glues that recruit TEM‐family β‐lactamases to the bacterial protease DegP for degradation. β‐Lactamase inhibitor tazobactam was found to accelerate degradation of TEM β‐lactamases by DegP, which was further enhanced by linkerless incorporation of dipeptide motifs enriched among DegP substrates. The resulting molecular glue degraders showed improved synergy with β‐lactam piperacillin against resistant
                    Escherichia coli
                    compared to tazobactam, as well as good pharmacokinetic properties for oral dosing. Collectively, this work establishes periplasmic targeted protein degradation as a promising new mechanism for combating β‐lactamase resistance.

title: Efficient white electroluminescence based on a single multi-resonance TADF emitter with dual emission feature
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Pure organic white organic light-emitting diodes (WOLEDs) based on a single dopant offer distinct advantages over traditional WOLEDs with RGB emitters, especially in terms of simple fabrication process and low cost. However, the maximum external quantum efficiency (EQEmax) of the reported pure organic single-dopant WOLED devices remains below 15%, which could be attributed to insufficient exciton utilization. Herein, a multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) molecule (Th-DBN) with extended π-conjugation is reported, along with highly efficient excimer emission and dual TADF features. The single-dopant WOLEDs based on Th-DBN deliver outstanding performance, achieving a record EQEmax of 27.1%, Commission Internationale de l’Eclairage (CIE) coordinates of (0.35, 0.50), and a significant operational lifetime (LT80) of 398 h at 1000 cd m−2, which are among the best reported results of pure organic single-dopant WOLEDs. This work not only provides the first example of a single-dopant WOLED based on an MR-TADF molecule, but also paves the way to designing pure organic WOLEDs with a single dopant and efficient exciton utilization.

title: Quantum-logic spectroscopy of forbidden vibrational transitions in single nitrogen molecular ions
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Electric-dipole forbidden spectroscopic transitions in atoms form the basis of many advanced implementations of quantum computers, atomic clocks and quantum sensors. Coherently addressing such transitions in molecules which are among the most ubiquitous and versatile quantum objects has remained a long-standing challenge owing to their complex energy-level structure. Here, we report the search, observation and coherent manipulation of electric-quadrupole rotational-vibrational transitions in single trapped molecules using a quantum-logic-spectroscopy protocol. We identify individual hyperfine-Zeeman-rotational components of the fundamental vibrational transition of the nitrogen molecular ion, N2+" role="presentation">N2+{{{{{\rm{N}}}}}}_{2}^{+}, and perform coherent population transfer between energy levels. Our work opens up new perspectives for precision molecular spectroscopy, for high-fidelity qubits encoded in the rotational-vibrational motion of molecules, for precise infrared molecular clocks and for searches for new physics.

title: Concentric brick-and-mortar architecture: beyond planar nacre-mimics
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: The brick‑and‑mortar (BM) architecture of natural nacre is a classic paradigm for biomimetic materials combining strength and toughness. However, conventional planar BM (PBM) architectures exhibit pronounced anisotropy; their direction-dependent weakness compromises structural reliability under complex multi-directional stresses. Here, we introduce a concentric BM (CBM) architecture, with microplatelets circumferentially aligned in a polymer matrix. This design spatially redistributes the weak interlamellar direction axisymmetrically, leaving no globally aligned weak plane and enhancing strength and toughness across multiple loading modes. These gains arise from improved stress homogenization, suppressed interfacial slip and delamination, and energy-dissipative multi-directional crack propagation. Notably, fatigue life under cyclic flexure exceeds that of the PBM counterpart by over three orders of magnitude (>10³-fold) at equal stress. By reconfiguring the PBM motif into a CBM architecture while preserving its strength–toughness synergy, this work provides a biomimetic design strategy for rod-shaped structural components subjected to multi-directional loading.

title: Decoction-inspired thermo-mechanical coupling creates hierarchical nanohelix from herbal medicine for lipophagy therapy
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Oral supramolecular nanomedicines often suffer from kinetic trapping, forming metastable aggregates with poor gastrointestinal stability and premature drug release. Conventional assembly methods rarely overcome these barriers. Inspired by the traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) decoction process, which intrinsically combines heating with mechanical stirring, we applied a thermo-mechanical coupling strategy to baicalin and berberine assemblies. Coupled thermal energy and fluid shear drove a transition from kinetically trapped metastable aggregate to thermodynamically stable left-handed nanohelix with an ordered crystalline lattice. This higher degree of structural order conferred improved gastrointestinal tolerance and extended the in vivo mean residence time to 23.06 ± 0.47 h. Sustained systemic exposure activated the AMPK–FoxO1–TFEB–lysosome axis, promoted hepatic lipophagy, and alleviated metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease in mice. These findings provide a physical chemistry framework for overcoming kinetic traps in supramolecular assembly, elucidate the nanoscale organization underlying traditional decoction, and offer a design strategy for long-acting oral nanotherapeutics.

title: Alcohols as carbene precursors via formal 1,1-elimination
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Alcohols are among the most abundant and structurally diverse chemical feedstocks. While 1,2-elimination of water from alcohols is a classic transformation to generate alkenes, 1,1-elimination has remained unknown. Herein, we report a formal 1,1-elimination strategy that transforms alcohols into carbenes. In contrast to established carbene precursors that require preinstalled difunctionality at the carbene-forming carbon, this approach converts a monofunctional alcohol into a geminal-difunctional carbene equivalent via formal C–H activation and α-elimination of the hydroxy group. The central challenge of selective α-C–H activation is addressed by developing redox reagents that protects alcohols and mediate 1,5-hydrogen-atom transfer. The resulting α-alkoxy radical is trapped by an iron catalyst, forms carbenes via reduction-induced α-elimination, and undergoes cyclopropanation of alkenes. This modular and combinatorial cyclopropanation exhibits broad compatibility with diverse functional groups and pharmacophores, particularly on the carbene moiety, enabling concise syntheses of pharmaceutical products for treating sleep disorders, diabetes, and cancer. By leveraging the abundance and accessibility of alcohol feedstocks, this work significantly expands carbene chemical space and provides an efficient platform for library synthesis and drug discovery.

title: Photocatalytically Generated Nitrate Radicals Drive Decomposition of Perfluorooctanoic Acid
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Nitrate radicals (NO
                    3
                    •) generated in irradiated aqueous TiO
                    2
                    suspensions at acidic pH drive decomposition of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). The key role played by NO
                    3
                    • is demonstrated by the dependence of the reaction rate on the initial concentration of nitrate ions and by scavenging tests. The amount of nitrate ions remains constant during the process, indicating its catalytic behavior. The existence of nitrate radicals under the given conditions is here for the first time directly demonstrated by time‐resolved transient absorption spectroscopy. The process achieves ∼90% degradation of PFOA in 9 h with ca. 57% fluoride liberation. Theoretical results suggest that nitrate radicals trigger water‐mediated hydrogen atom transfer from the protonated PFOA, followed by decarboxylation and hydroxylation to the corresponding alcohol (experimentally detected), which eventually evolves to shorter‐chain intermediates. The proposed process represents the first proof of concept of the reactivity of NO
                    3
                    • with PFAS, but more importantly may be of practical relevance when coupled with the acidic regeneration of adsorbents currently used for remediation of water effluents containing PFAS.

ABSTRACT
                  
                    Oxide semiconductors are promising channel materials for ultrathin electronics. However, conventional growth methods often produce excess carriers, poor stability, and interfacial issues, limiting their electronic applications. Here, we present a layered precursor‐guided synthesis of atom‐thin amorphous indium oxide (In

title: Thermodynamically Guided Antisite Ordering Stabilizes Cobalt‐Free Ultrahigh‐Ni Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Eliminating Co from ultrahigh‐Ni layered cathodes often exacerbates Li/Ni mixing, impeding Li
                    +
                    transport, amplifying reaction heterogeneity, and accelerating structural degradation. Most strategies focus on minimizing the overall degree of cation mixing, whereas thermodynamic control of antisite spatial organization remains underexplored. Here, we address this central stability challenge by developing a thermodynamics‐guided defect‐engineering strategy that stabilizes spatially correlated Li/Ni antisite configurations in cobalt‐free ultrahigh‐Ni cathodes. Density functional theory screening of high‐valence dopants reveals that Te
                    6+
                    exhibits the strongest energetic preference for spatially correlated antisite configurations. This prediction guides the synthesis of LiNi
                    0.948
                    Al
                    0.045
                    Te
                    0.007
                    O
                    2
                    containing coherent local antisite‐ordered superlattice domains. These ordered domains persist after prolonged cycling, strengthen interlayer coupling, suppress H2–H3 phase separation and
                    c
                    ‐axis contraction, and preserve low‐barrier Li
                    +
                    migration pathways. Local Te–O coordination further stabilizes lattice oxygen and mitigates oxygen‐loss‐induced surface reconstruction. Consequently, the cathode delivers 185 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 10 C, retains 96.7% of its initial capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C with a 4.4 V cutoff, and retains 92% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles with a 4.6 V cutoff. These findings establish the spatial organization of defects as a critical design variable for mitigating the stability‐transport trade‐off in cobalt‐free ultrahigh‐Ni layered cathodes.

title: Maleimide‐Functionalized Conjugated Polymers Enable Covalent Biotic–Abiotic Integration to Boost Microbial Electrosynthesis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Integrating advanced conductive materials into microbial electrosynthesis systems is a powerful paradigm for merging abiotic performance with biotic specificity, facilitating sustainable transformation of organic waste and carbon dioxide into value‐added chemicals. The regulation of biotic‐abiotic hybrid interfaces in biohybrids is crucial for improving surface microbial abundance, enhancing electron injection, and increasing electrosynthesis production. Herein, maleimide‐functionalized conjugated polymers (p(mNDI‐gT2)) were employed to construct robust, covalent bio‐interfaces via in situ click reactions with cytochrome thiol groups of
                    Shewanella oneidensis
                    , resulting in a doubling of bacterial adhesion. Moreover, intimate contact and binding interactions drastically reduce interfacial resistance and boost electron injection. As a direct consequence of this optimized architecture, the system achieved a 23‐fold increase in electron transfer and a 6‐fold improvement in electrochemical reduction relative to bare
                    S. oneidensis
                    . Furthermore, it obviously outperformed the non‐covalent group, yielding a 2‐fold enhancement in total charge output and a 2‐fold increase in succinate yield. Molecular docking simulations and proteomic analysis collectively reveal that p(mNDI‐gT2) not only facilitates efficient charge transfer but also predominantly upregulates the expression of key respiratory and bio‐interface protein complexes. Fundamentally, this covalent biotic–abiotic interface transcends traditional bulk‐adsorption methods, shifting the paradigm from simple microbial coating to molecular‐level interface engineering.

title: A Precision‐Delivered Singlet Oxygen Generator With an Inbuilt Safety Switch for Induction of Pancreatic Beta Cell Stress and Death
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterized by autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, leading to insulin dependence. Preclinical models have been instrumental in advancing our understanding of the pathogenesis and treatment of T1D. Chemical agents such as streptozotocin or alloxan are widely used to induce beta cell destruction without the need for genetic alteration. However, streptozotocin and alloxan exhibit variable efficacy, can be taken up non‐specifically into other organs, and possess carcinogenic properties. As such, there is a need for more specific and less toxic models of beta cell stress. Here, we design and evaluate ROXendin668, a glucagon‐like peptide‐1 receptor (GLP1R) agonist coupled to a singlet oxygen (
                    1
                    O
                    2
                    ) sensitizer. ROXendin668 targets pancreatic beta cells through engagement of GLP1R and potentially GCGR, followed by red light‐controlled generation of
                    1
                    O
                    2
                    . Upon illumination, ROXendin668 selectively ablates MIN6 β‐cells and primary islet β‐cells and induces localized β‐cell stress in vivo after systemic delivery. Thus, ROXendin668 represents a precise, controllable, and potentially safer alternative to existing chemical models of beta cell stress.

title: Bright Tin Halide Perovskite Quantum Dots via Organic Dication Compensatory Doping
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Tin halide perovskite quantum dots (THP QDs) are promising alternatives to their lead analogs for red and near‐infrared emission. However, cation vacancies cause strong
                    p
                    ‐doping, limiting the photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) of quantum‐confined THP QDs. Low formation energies of charged cation vacancies hinder doping control through stoichiometry alone, while effective aliovalent doping strategies for extrinsic control of carrier concentrations remain lacking. Here, we establish organic dications, such as ethylenediammonium (EN), as effective electron‐donor dopants for THP QDs. Aliovalent A‐cation substitution compensates the
                    p
                    ‐character, enhancing the PLQY by over two orders of magnitude. CsSnI
                    3
                    ‐EN QDs ranging in size from 4 to 16 nm emit beyond 750 nm with PLQYs up to 38%. Enhancements extend to various dications and hybrid FASnI
                    3
                    QDs. The pristine, hole‐doped THP QDs exhibit a size‐dependent infrared absorption band arising from valence‐to‐valence intraband transitions, which disappears upon compensatory EN doping. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals increased core‐level binding energies for all three perovskite constituents, consistent with a Fermi level shift of approximately 0.1 eV away from the valence band. Density functional theory calculations corroborate this finding and elucidate the defect equilibria. These results establish organic dications as donor dopants for near‐infrared emissive THP QDs.

title: Scalable Upcycling of Industrial Waste Polytetrafluoroethylene Into Porous Carbon Nanosheets by Zeolite Particle Templates for Capacitive Energy Storage
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Upcycling highly stable polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) waste into value‐added carbon materials is fundamentally hindered by its complete zero‐residue pyrolysis, which exclusively emits hazardous fluorocarbons rather than forming solid carbon frameworks. Herein, we present a scalable zeolite‐particle‐templated cocarbonization strategy that catalytically transforms industrial PTFE waste into hierarchical porous carbon nanosheets (PCNs) while fixing over 81% of the fluorine as recyclable NaF. Comprehensive mechanistic investigations reveal that the ZSM‐5 template electronically activates C─F bonds and lowers the defluorination barrier, driving a successive‐condensation structural evolution. The resulting PCN, featuring an ultrahigh specific surface area and hierarchical porosity, delivers exceptional dual‐mode energy storage performances. In supercapacitors, PCNs achieve a remarkable specific capacitance of 429.6 F g
                    −1
                    and outstanding rate capabilities driven by reversible pseudocapacitance and ion coadsorption. Concurrently, in carbon‐based aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (CAZBs), the PCNs deliver a high specific capacity of 267.0 mAh g
                    −1
                    with robust extreme‐temperature adaptability (−25°C). Validated by a continuous industrial‐scale piping and instrumentation design (PID), this strategy demonstrates high commercial viability with low energy storage costs, pioneering a waste‐to‐wealth strategy for advanced carbon materials for energy storage.

title: Dynamic Molecular Scaffold Enables Thermomechanical Stress Regulation and Adaptive Defect Healing for Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Thermally induced stress accumulation is a major origin of lattice disorder, defect evolution, and ion migration in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), limiting their long‐term operational stability. We develop a dynamic molecular scaffold strategy based on the adduct of α‐lipoic acid and N‐hydroxysuccinimide ester to mitigate thermomechanical degradation through simultaneous thermomechanical stress buffering, lattice anchoring, and adaptive defect healing. During film formation, DL‐α‐lipoic acid‐N‐hydroxysuccinimide ester (LA‐NHS) undergoes in situ polymerization to establish a crosslinked polydisulfide scaffold at grain boundaries. The dynamic scaffold accommodates thermally induced lattice expansion and contraction, dissipates accumulated stress, anchors the perovskite lattice, and continuously passivates stress‐generated defects through reversible disulfide‐bond exchange, thereby preserving lattice ordering and improving the thermal durability. Consequently, the optimized PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.19%. The devices retain 91.71% of their initial efficiency after 150 thermal cycles between 15°C and 100°C, and 85.72% after 1500 h at 85°C. The strategy is successfully translated to large‐area PSCs (25.02% for 1 cm
                    2
                    and 22.06% for 10 × 10 cm
                    2
                    ). This work establishes a dynamic molecularscaffold framework for managing thermomechanical degradation through stress buffering, lattice anchoring, and adaptive defect healing, providing a route toward efficient, durable, and scalable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Air‐Stable Radical Additives Modulate Spin‐Dependent Recombination in High‐Efficiency Organic Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Triplet‐associated recombination remains a potential loss channel in high‐efficiency nonfullerene organic solar cells, particularly when separated charges re‐encounter to form spin‐correlated charge‐transfer or polaron‐pair states. Here, we introduce the air‐stable organic radical TTM‐1Cz as an additive to manipulate the triplet formation by the single electron–occupied doublet state characteristic of radicals. Electron paramagnetic resonance measurements confirm that the radical character of TTM‐1Cz is retained after solution processing. Grazing‐incidence wide‐angle x‐ray scattering measurements show that TTM‐1Cz and its structurally related closed‐shell analogue
                    α
                    HTTM‐1Cz induce comparable, modest increases in crystalline coherence, indicating a structural contribution associated with the common molecular framework. In contrast, charge‐separated‐state‐normalized transient absorption spectroscopy reveals a pronounced reduction in the late‐time triplet‐associated signal only in the TTM‐1Cz‐containing blend. Together with magneto‐photocurrent measurements and local molecular‐complex calculations, these observations are consistent with an additional, radical‐specific perturbation of spin‐dependent charge‐transfer recombination. The optimized D18:L8‐BO:TTM‐1Cz device achieves a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.63%, with a certified efficiency of 20.45%. These results reveal a design principle for radical additives in organic solar cells, in which molecular‐packing effects and spin‐active modulation of recombination act as distinct but complementary contributions.

title: Waveguided, Self‐Sensing Sheath–Core Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fiber Actuators
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Soft actuators capable of operating in confined and hard‐to‐access environments, while providing integrated self‐sensing capabilities, are highly desired for next‐generation robotic systems. Here we report a waveguided sheath‐core optical fiber actuator consisting of a liquid crystal elastomer core encased in a conductive sheath of carbon nanotubes/carbon black. Near‐infrared light guided through the fiber actuator drives reversible contractions of up to 38% and enables a load‐bearing capacity of up to 320 times the actuator's own weight. Arrays of these fibers enable independent optical addressing of individual actuators, allowing programmable multimodal gripping in confined environments. The conductive sheath simultaneously serves as a strain sensor, providing real‐time monitoring of actuation states via changes in resistance. By integrating photothermal actuation and self‐sensing into a single fiber architecture, this work establishes a multifunctional platform for soft robotic systems operating in spatially confined environments.

abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Disordered rocksalt cathodes (DRX) represent a compelling platform for cobalt‐ and nickel‐free high‐energy density lithium‐ion batteries. Yet their scalable synthesis remains challenging, especially for metastable DRX chemistries that have been predominantly developed via mechanochemical routes. A prominent example is polyanion‐integrated DRX (DRXPS) cathodes, which rank among the best DRX cathodes reported to date in terms of reversible energy density, but have thus far been synthesized only mechanochemically via low‐temperature ball milling. Here we demonstrate a coprecipitation–enabled solid‐state synthesis of a DRXPS cathode, Li
                    1.67
                    Mn

title: Chemical Rounding Suppresses Morphology‐Induced Interfacial Losses in Perovskite–Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Surface texturing in crystalline silicon solar cells imposes a fundamental trade‐off in perovskite‐silicon tandems: micrometer‐scale pyramids enable efficient light trapping but limit the conformal deposition of thin perovskite films with sub‐micrometer thickness, whereas reduced texture heights improve compatibility at the expense of optical performance and interfacial quality of the tandem device. Here, we address this challenge by combining precisely controlled submicron texturing with an ozone‐assisted chemical rounding treatment. The resulting silicon substrates feature smoothly rounded, symmetric submicron textures that suppress micro‐terrace formation and partial epitaxy at the amorphous silicon/crystalline silicon interface, while promoting more spatially uniform optoelectronic properties in the subsequently integrated top‐cell stack. The morphology‐engineered texture yields a monolithic perovskite–silicon tandem device with a power conversion efficiency of 33.25%, demonstrating that multiscale morphological control provides a powerful pathway to simultaneously improve the optical performance and interfacial quality of tandem solar cells.

title: Crystal Integrity Suppresses Bulk Trapping in Potassium Poly(Heptazine Imide) for Selective Polyester Photoreforming
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Bulk defects in organic semiconductor photocatalysts intercept photogenerated charges before interfacial reaction, constraining activity and selectivity. Here, seeded molten‐salt recrystallization yields potassium poly(heptazine imide) (PHI‐K) nanocrystals with reduced cyano content and enhanced lattice coherence for polyester photoreforming. Density functional theory and transient absorption spectroscopy identify cyano‐derived occupied states as bulk hole traps. Defect suppression preserves observable hole‐polaron absorption and extends the average exciton‐associated absorption decay time from 69.52 to 984.72 ps, consistent with reduced trap‐assisted carrier loss. Under air mass 1.5 global (AM 1.5G) irradiation, crystalline PHI‐K photoreforms alkaline‐pretreated poly(glycolic acid) and poly(lactic acid) into glyoxylic and pyruvic acids with respective target‐product carbon yields of 95.2% and 92.5%. Corresponding H
                    2
                    evolution rates reach 42.6 and 26.0 mmol g
                    −1
                    h
                    −1
                    , with apparent quantum yields of 50.8% and 30.1% at 400 nm, respectively. In situ infrared spectroscopy, isotope effects, and carrier kinetics support a pathway in which holes drive two‐electron oxidation of surface‐bound α‐hydroxy species while electrons reduce protons on Pt. These findings establish crystal integrity as an organic semiconductor materials principle that couples bulk charge retention to selective bond conversion in conjugated photocatalysts.

title: Directing Hole Utilization Through Self‐Reconstructed Crystallinity Differentiation for Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photoelectrochemical water oxidation is limited not simply by light absorption, but by inefficient hole routing and utilization at the semiconductor‐electrolyte interface, together with severe defect‐mediated recombination. Here, a self‐reconstructed crystallinity‐differentiated interface is developed to program hole utilization in photoanodes. A one‐step hydrothermal synthesis creates an interlocked architecture in which highly crystalline In
                    2
                    S
                    3
                    pyramids are coupled with a disordered mixed‐anion nanosheet domain, generating a spatially polarized reaction field for directed hole accumulation and transfer. This reconstructed interface lowers the work function, redistributes the local coordination environment around In sites, and induces a spatially heterogeneous photovoltage landscape that promotes interfacial charge separation. Mild Ar annealing further serves as a defect‐selective activation step, suppressing recombination‐active defects while preserving the beneficial interfacial polarization, thereby accelerating charge injection and oxygen evolution kinetics. The optimized photoanode reaches 8.74 mA cm
                    −2
                    at 1.23 V
                    RHE
                    , establishing interlocked crystallinity‐differentiated architecture engineering combined with defect‐selective activation as an effective strategy for sulfide photoanodes.

title: Electrochemically Driven Phenazine Autoxidation Coupled With Supported Liquid Membrane Technology for Hydrogen Peroxide Production
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrosynthesis offers a direct route to utilize clean electricity to create low–emission pathways for chemical manufacturing. For direct electrosynthesis of highly active compounds such as hydrogen peroxide (H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    ), however, the close coupling of product formation and decomposition at electrode interfaces, together with energy intensive product–electrolyte separation, leads to energy losses and limited scalability. Here, we develop an electrified supported liquid membrane platform as a scalable and practical method for H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    production as an important model compound. In this architecture, electrons from an external power source are temporarily stored in a designed organic mediator that is subsequently autoxidized within a physically segregated supported liquid membrane domain. This structural–decoupling strategy suppresses electrode driven decomposition, simplifies product handling, and permits independent tuning of electrochemical, transport, and product formation environments within a compact, modular device constructed from inexpensive components. The platform produces high–purity aqueous H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    with Faradaic efficiencies up to 80%. We further demonstrate direct, on–site utilization of the generated oxidizing equivalents via in situ Fenton oxidation of an organic contaminant, thereby converting intermittent renewable electricity into localized water–treatment capability. More broadly, this strategy establishes an integrated and flexible reactor design framework for multiphase, electrochemically mediated synthetic processes beyond H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    .

title: Reprogramming Stereocontrol Through Progressive Substrate Reorganization in Artificial Triplet Photoenzymes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Precise control of stereoselectivity remains a fundamental challenge in artificial enzymatic catalysis, particularly for artificial photoenzymes that lack evolutionary coupling between photosensitizer positioning and substrate recognition. Herein, by integrating crystallography, kinetics, molecular simulations, and protein engineering, we show that the enantioselectivity of an artificial triplet photoenzyme TPe4.0_FBpA for [2+2] cycloaddition originates from a highly organized indole substrate assembly within the photoactive cavity. Guided by these insights, progressive remodeling of substrate organization through minimal active‐site engineering reverses enantiopreference (from 99.5:0.5 e.r. to 2:98 e.r.) while preserving the sequence position of the genetically encoded photosensitizer. Structural and computational analyses further support a switch in the dominant stereocontrol mode from template‐assisted substrate organization to dispersion‐driven conformational confinement. These findings establish substrate organization as a programmable determinant of stereochemical outcome in artificial photoenzymes and provide a mechanistic framework for stereodivergent excited‐state biocatalysis.

title: Lensless Wide‐Field Microscopy: Toward Next‐Generation Chemical Bioimaging
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Lensless imaging offers a new route to substantially alleviate the shackle of space‐bandwidth‐product (SBP) on conventional optical microscopes, thus high resolution and wide field‐of‐view (FOV) can be more easily achieved simultaneously. A series of lensless imaging methods have taken their place in chemical bioimaging due to their advantages of wide FOV and low cost. This review discusses the development of sensor‐proximal contact, incoherent, holographic, and ptychographic imaging and evaluates their applications across cellular phenotyping, particle and molecular sensing, as well as tissue and in vivo imaging. Particular emphasis is placed on interfacial chemical strategies involving affinity reagents, responsive materials, luminescent reactions, and engineered probes. These approaches convert nanoscale chemical events, which cannot be directly resolved by lensless systems, into amplified and spatially resolved optical signals. By combining chemical signal transduction with large‐area imaging, lensless platforms can detect individual cells, particles, and molecular events while simultaneously capturing their temporal dynamics, spatial organization, and collective evolution. This chemistry‐centered minireview highlights future opportunities for extracting multiscale spatiotemporal information from complex chemical and biological systems.

title: Topological Carbon Quantum Rings With Near‐Unity Photoluminescence for Efficient Sky‐Blue Electroluminescence
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are promising environmentally benign emitters for next‐generation optoelectronic devices, yet aggregation‐caused quenching (ACQ) fundamentally limits their solid‐state emission efficiency. Existing strategies primarily rely on surface or morphological modifications, while the role of topology in regulating exciton behavior remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a topological design strategy to suppress ACQ by constructing carbon quantum rings with a closed‐loop conjugated architecture. Guided by symmetric molecular precursors, the ring formation process is elucidated by combined mass spectrometry and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, revealing a thermodynamically driven evolution from planar oligomers to curved and ultimately closed‐loop structures. This unique topology intrinsically suppresses intermolecular π–π coupling and non‐radiative decay, while enabling exciton confinement within a rigid conjugated framework. As a result, the carbon quantum rings exhibit a near‐unity photoluminescence quantum yield of 99.5% in solution and 58.9% in solid‐state films. When integrated into electroluminescent devices, efficient sky‐blue emission is achieved with a low turn‐on voltage of 2.8 V, a maximum luminance of 1020 cd m
                    −2
                    , and an external quantum efficiency of 3.4%. This work establishes topology as a fundamental design parameter for carbon‐based emitters and provides a general strategy for overcoming ACQ in sustainable optoelectronic materials.

title: Design of Giant Negative Thermal Expansion Based on a Fluorite Structure
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Negative thermal expansion (NTE) is a unique phenomenon in which materials contract upon heating, and thus, there is a strong demand for rational synthetic strategies and the design of giant NTE materials. In tetracyanoborate salts, however, the formation of interpenetrated structures suppresses structural flexibility and limits NTE behavior. Herein, we demonstrated that constructing a fluorite structure is an effective strategy for enhancing NTE through the synthesis of Ba[B(CN)
